result.topic_en: Draft of the argument on the conditions for the existence of the definite integral (convergence of the sum S as the interval lengths shrink), its extension to functions that become infinite at isolated points, and the proof that a bounded function with finitely many maxima and minima is integrable.

methods.what: Splitting the oscillation sum into intervals with oscillation > σ (total length s) and the rest, bounding by s times the total oscillation plus σ(b−a)
methods.quote:
Denn diejenigen Intervalle, in denen die Schwankungen $>\sigma$ sind,
liefern zur Summe
$\delta_1 D_1 + \delta_2 D_2 \dots$

methods.what: Choosing σ first, then interval size d so s is small, making the oscillation sum arbitrarily small, so S converges (integrability criterion)
methods.quote: Offenbar kann man nun {+erst+} $\sigma$ beliebig klein annehmen

methods.what: Extension of the integral to functions becoming infinite at isolated points via a limit of the integration bounds (improper integral)
methods.quote:

immer endlich sei, aber tritt die Bedingung, daß die Function
nur bei Annäherung an einzelne {+Argumentwerthe+} [-Werthe-] unendlich
werde

methods.what: For a monotone increasing function with all δ<d, the oscillation sum is bounded by d(f(b)−f(a)), hence monotone bounded functions are integrable

items.english: We have thus found conditions that are necessary and sufficient for the sum to converge as the quantities δ decrease indefinitely.

items.quote:
bemerken wir zuerst, daß [-die Summe-]
$S$ immer convergirt, wenn die Function {+$f(x)$+} immer endlich
ist und nicht unendlich viele Maxima und Minima
hat.
items.english: We remark first that S always converges if the function f(x) is always finite and does not have infinitely many maxima and minima.

items.quote:
Eine Function, welche nicht unendlich viele Maxima
und Minima hat, kann daher nur, wo sie unendlich wird,
der Integration unfähig sein.
items.english: A function which does not have infinitely many maxima and minima can therefore be incapable of integration only where it becomes infinite.
